🇲🇽💵 <u>Higher Wages, More on the Plate: Mexico's Meat Consumption Up 27%</u>

Mexico has logged five straight years of rising meat consumption, from 9.06 million tons in 2020 to 11.55 million in 2025. That's a 27% jump. And it's the producers themselves giving the credit: minimum-wage policy, social programs, the anti-inflation package (PACIC) and remittances. Between January and October 2026, consumer chicken prices fell 4.5% and pork 2.8%.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>Citi: Mexico Set to Win From the AI Boom</u>

Citi Research's "LatAm Poised for Take-Off" report names Mexico one of the main winners of North America's supply-chain reshuffle: it has gained share of US imports and locked in its place as Washington's No. 1 trading partner, El Economista reports. The driver is AI. Mexican exports of CPUs, assembled from Taiwanese and other Asian parts and shipped north, have been a major source of that gain. Citi's caveat: a pipeline of investment projects is waiting for clarity on the T-MEC review.
banner: CITI: MEXICO WINS FROM AI BOOM

🇲🇽🚆 <u>Rizo de Oro Bridge Opens in Chiapas</u>

Sheinbaum opened the Rizo de Oro steel-arch bridge in La Concordia, Chiapas: 2.308 billion pesos, 2 km long, more than 5,700 jobs during construction, and 300,000 people served, El Soberano reports. The trip between Tuxtla Gutiérrez and Frontera Comalapa drops from over five hours to about two and a half. Criminal threats in the Frailesca and Sierra regions halted the work more than once. It opened anyway.
banner: CHIAPAS: RIZO DE ORO BRIDGE OPENS

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Inés Gómez Mont: 2.45 Billion Pesos Through Ghost Companies</u>

Mexico's Attorney General Ernestina Godoy laid out the scheme: about 2.45 billion pesos in 2016–2017 contracts from Peña Nieto's federal prison agency (OADPRS) went to ghost companies issuing fake invoices, and the money allegedly landed in the personal bank accounts of TV host Inés Gómez Mont. She faces three federal arrest warrants, including for organized crime and money laundering. Extradition from the US for her and her husband, Víctor Manuel Álvarez Puga, is still pending.
banner: GÓMEZ MONT: 2.45B PESOS VIA GHOST FIRMS

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Fox Confesses 2006 — and the PAN Runs</u>

For 20 years Mexico's right called the 2006 fraud a fantasy. Now Vicente Fox admits he intervened to put Felipe Calderón in power and says he never would have handed the presidential sash to López Obrador. The PAN, which had brought him back as a voice for the next election, suddenly wants nothing to do with him. "When we denounced the 2006 fraud, they called us crazy," Sheinbaum said. "We always said Calderón was a spurious president, and we still do. Now Fox proves us right."

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Big Taxpayers' Debt to SAT Falls 58 Billion Pesos</u>

Tax debts owed to Mexico's SAT by large taxpayers (companies and individuals earning over 1.5 billion pesos a year) fell 58.18 billion pesos, or 4.9%, in a year: from 1.176 trillion to 1.118 trillion pesos, La Jornada reports. Audits of big taxpayers brought in 208.7 billion pesos through September, roughly double the target. Under Calderón and Peña Nieto, the same club got tax pardons instead.
banner: SAT: BIG DEBTORS OWE 58B PESOS LESS

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>Dos Bocas Output Up 12.7% Year-on-Year</u>

Pemex's Olmeca refinery at Dos Bocas averaged 215,000 barrels per day of fuels in September, up 12.7% from 192,000 a year earlier, La Jornada reports. It's the refinery's third straight month above 200,000 bpd, after an August record of 270,000, and it now supplies more than a fifth of Pemex's 1.029 million bpd of fuel output. The plant they swore would never refine a drop.
